learningObjectives.text: Explain this episode: Whose death changes Achilles’ decision to fight?
Use the cited passage to explain: What makes the borrowed armour important?

main.author: Homer
main.locator: Book 18, news of Patroclus’ death; Book 18, normalized characters 0-300
main.excerpt: The grief of Achilles over Patroclus—The visit of Thetis to Vulcan and the armour that he made for Achilles. Thus then did they fight as it were a flaming fire. Meanwhile the fleet runner Antilochus, who had been sent as messenger, reached Achilles, and found him sitting by his tall ships and boding
main.note: Verbatim local text with whitespace normalized. Lesson analysis is interpretation, not part of this quotation.

narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: Patroclus fights in Achilles’ armour and is killed. News of his death turns Achilles from withdrawal toward vengeance against Hector; the return to battle grows out of bereavement, not a successful settlement by gifts.

narrativeBlocks.title: What the source does
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (translation; whitespace normalized): “The grief of Achilles over Patroclus—The visit of Thetis to Vulcan and the armour that he made for Achilles. Thus then did they fight as it were a flaming fire. Meanwhile the fleet runner Antilochus, who had been sent as messenger, reached Achilles, and found him sitting by his tall ships and boding”

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: Interpretation: The borrowed armor concentrates the poem’s tragedy: heroic identity can help others for a moment, but it cannot transfer fate.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read it carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: Track the change in motive: Achilles’ anger at Agamemnon does not simply vanish, but grief for Patroclus makes vengeance against Hector urgent. Returning to battle is not the same as being healed.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: The next question is whether grief can produce compassion as well as vengeance.

quiz.prompt: Whose death changes Achilles’ decision to fight?
quiz.explanation: Patroclus’. Revisit the named passage and distinguish its narrative from the lesson’s interpretation.

quiz.prompt: What makes the borrowed armour important?

choices.text: It proves Hector has already accepted a truce.
It links Patroclus’ intervention to Achilles’ absent role.
It makes Patroclus immune to divine interference.
